solves: Shows the calendar of a person or a group as events in the work week, week, day, month and list views, on desktop and on a phone, so the person sees what is coming, finds a time and opens an event, while the screen owns the detail, the creation and the editing of the event.
use_when: The person needs to see what is coming in a week, a day or a month and to find a free time: the work week with the side panel, the view the piece opens in.
The person plans by the month: the month view, with the events in a row per day and +N more when they do not fit.
The person reads the events in sequence, or uses a screen reader: the list view.
The screen is a phone: below 768 px of the width of the element the piece is the compact month with the list of the chosen day.
Several calendars share one grid and the person turns each one on and off in My calendars: give each calendar its color.
The screen opens the detail of an event beside it: put the content in the detail slot and open it with open-event.
do_not_use_when: To choose a date in a form: use the date picker, not the scheduler.
For tasks with no time of day: use a list or a table.
To mark an event by status, such as error, warning or success: the color of an event is the choice of the calendar, never a status.
To show a cancelled event only by color: the piece writes Cancelled: and strikes the title, and keeps it in the grid.
To open the detail, create or edit an event inside the piece: that belongs to the screen, which gets the click on the event.
For past or tentative events, a time scale or the arrow keys on the grid: they are outside this version.

events.constraint: Property only, and the screen owns it. The events, as a list of { id, title, start, end, allDay, calendar, cancelled, recurring, people }. id (unique) and title are required. start and end are wall-clock text, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, or YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day event, whose end is the last day, included; a text with a time zone is refused. end absent: the event ends when it starts. calendar is the id of a calendar, which gives the color and the name; absent, the color is primary and the event has no calendar name. cancelled and recurring are booleans. people is a list of { name, src }, shown as avatars in the day header and in the list row. An event that cannot be drawn, such as a repeated id, a date that does not exist, an end before the start or a calendar that does not exist, is left out and emits console.error in development, one per cause. The empty state is not a property: it is a period with no visible event.

calendars.constraint: Property only. The calendars, as a list of { id, name, color, visible }. id (unique), name and color are required. color is primary or one of sistemas, gerencial, educacao, comercial, financeiro, igrejas and rh, equal in every brand and never a status. visible is true by default; false hides the events of the calendar. The checkbox of My calendars turns it on and off: the piece replaces calendars with a new list and never changes the objects of the screen. A calendar that cannot be drawn is left out and emits console.error in development.

labels.constraint: Property only. Every text the piece writes, already localized by the screen, as one object with the keys listed below as labels.<key>. The piece writes no word of its own. A missing label renders anyway and emits console.error in development, once, saying which keys are missing. Placeholders are written between braces: count and date.

filter-items.constraint: Property only. The property is filterItems. The items of the Filter menu, as the items of nph-dropdown-menu. Without them the Filter button only fires nph-filter-click.

view.constraint: The Figma property `vista`. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the layout by it. The piece writes it when the person changes the view and fires nph-view-change; setting it from code fires nothing. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development. On a phone the view stays the compact month, whatever the value.

date.constraint: The day the period is built around, YYYY-MM-DD. Absent, today. The piece writes it when the person moves the period and fires nph-date-change; setting it from code fires nothing. A date that does not exist draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

week-start.constraint: The property is weekStart. The first day of the week. It is not taken from the language. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

hide-side-panel.constraint: The inverse of the Figma boolean `lateral`. Hides the side panel, with the mini month and My calendars, in every desktop view; the sidebar button in the toolbar toggles the same panel, writes this attribute and fires nph-side-panel-change. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the grid by it. The phone has no side panel.

loading.constraint: Skeleton rows in the place of the events; the toolbar stays active and the week keeps its days. The events area is marked busy and the loading label is announced. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the loading look by it.

now.constraint: An instant, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, that stands for the clock: the now line and today are the same in a story and a test. Absent, the clock of the machine, read again every minute. An instant that does not exist draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

open-event.constraint: The property is openEvent. The id of the event whose detail is open. The piece writes it when the person opens an event and takes the attribute off when the detail closes. With content in the detail slot it opens the nph-popover beside the event, with the title of the event as heading, and writes aria-expanded true on the event. Without content in the slots nothing opens. Reflects so the page can see which detail is open.

labels.today.constraint: The text of the Today button, which goes to the current day.

labels.previous.constraint: The accessible name of the previous period button.

labels.next.constraint: The accessible name of the next period button.

labels.newEvent.constraint: The text of the New event button on desktop and its accessible name on a phone, where the button is icon only.

labels.filter.constraint: The text of the Filter button and the accessible name of its menu.

labels.sidePanel.constraint: The accessible name of the sidebar button, its tooltip and the name of the side panel.

labels.view.constraint: The accessible name of the view select.

labels.viewWorkWeek.constraint: The text of the work week option of the view select.

labels.viewWeek.constraint: The text of the week option of the view select.

labels.viewDay.constraint: The text of the day option of the view select.

labels.viewMonth.constraint: The text of the month option of the view select.

labels.viewList.constraint: The text of the list option of the view select.

labels.allDay.constraint: The label of the all-day band and the time of an all-day event in the lists and in the accessible name.

labels.cancelled.constraint: The text written before the struck title of a cancelled event, such as Cancelled:.

labels.cancelledName.constraint: The word that says cancelled in the accessible name of the event.

labels.repeats.constraint: The word that says the event repeats in the accessible name of the event.

labels.more.constraint: The text of the more button of a month cell, with the marker {count}, such as +{count} more.

labels.moreName.constraint: The accessible name of the group of the more button, with the markers {count} and {date}, such as {count} more events on {date}.

labels.myCalendars.constraint: The heading of the list of calendars in the side panel.

labels.miniPrevious.constraint: The accessible name of the previous month button of the mini month.

labels.miniNext.constraint: The accessible name of the next month button of the mini month.

labels.emptyTitle.constraint: The title of the empty state, such as No events this week.

labels.emptyHint.constraint: The hint of the empty state, below the title.

labels.loading.constraint: The status text announced while the events load.

labels.todayName.constraint: The word that says today in the accessible name of the current day.

nph-view-change.constraint: Fires when the person changes the view in the select or goes to the day view by +N more, with detail { view }. It bubbles and is composed. Setting view from code fires nothing.

nph-date-change.constraint: Fires when the person moves the date, with detail { date, source }. date is YYYY-MM-DD. source is today, previous, next, mini-month, month or more. It bubbles and is composed. Setting date from code fires nothing.

nph-event-click.constraint: Fires when the person activates an event, with detail { id, source }, source being pointer or keyboard. It bubbles, is composed and is cancelable: preventDefault keeps the detail from opening. The screen decides what the click does.

nph-event-close.constraint: Fires when the detail closes because of the person, with detail { id, source }. source is escape, outside, focus-out, toggle or close-button. It bubbles and is composed. Esc gives the focus back to the event.

nph-day-click.constraint: Fires when the person activates a day of the grid, with detail { date }. It bubbles and is composed. The piece does nothing else with the click: the screen decides.

nph-new-event.constraint: Fires when the person activates New event, with detail { date }, the day the period is built around. It bubbles and is composed. The piece creates no event.

nph-filter-click.constraint: Fires when the person activates Filter and filter-items is empty. It bubbles and is composed.

nph-filter-select.constraint: Fires when the person chooses an item of the Filter menu, with detail { value, checked }. checked is a boolean, or null for an item that has no selection. It bubbles and is composed.

nph-calendar-toggle.constraint: Fires when the person turns a calendar of My calendars on or off, with detail { id, visible }. It bubbles and is composed. The piece has already replaced calendars with a new list.

nph-side-panel-change.constraint: Fires when the person toggles the side panel with the sidebar button, with detail { open }. It bubbles and is composed. Setting hide-side-panel from code fires nothing.

detail.constraint: The body of the detail of the open event, drawn by the screen inside the nph-popover that the piece opens beside the event. The piece does not draw the detail: with no content in this slot and in detail-footer, an event opens nothing.

detail-footer.constraint: The actions of the detail, in the footer of the nph-popover, as nph-button elements. The divider comes with the footer.

view.choose_when: work-week, the default, to answer what the person has this week; week when the weekend matters; day for one day in hours; month to plan; list to read in sequence.
do_not_combine_with: a view outside the list: the piece draws nothing
another view on a phone: the compact month stays

screen.choose_when: desktop, with the toolbar, the side panel and the grid, when the element is 768 px wide or more; phone, the compact month with the list of the chosen day, below that. It is read from the element, not from the window.
do_not_combine_with: the side panel on a phone
Today, Filter and the sidebar button on a phone

side-panel.choose_when: shown, the default, in every desktop view, so the person changes the day in the mini month and turns calendars on and off; hidden when the screen needs the width.
do_not_combine_with: hide-side-panel on a phone: there is no panel to hide

event-color.choose_when: primary, the default, for the calendar with no color of its own; one of sistemas, gerencial, educacao, comercial, financeiro, igrejas or rh when the person tells calendars apart by color. The color belongs to the calendar and is equal in every brand.
do_not_combine_with: educacao together with primary in the brand Educacao, where they are the same color

event-type.choose_when: The height comes from the duration: one hour, a short event, a long event and an all-day or multi-day bar. A recurring event adds the repeat icon. The height never goes below the minimum target.
do_not_combine_with: a time with a time zone

week-start.choose_when: sunday, the default; monday when the people of the screen start the week there.

default.token: scheduler/background, scheduler/border, scheduler/border-width, scheduler/radius, scheduler/padding, scheduler/foreground
default.changes_for_user: The container with the toolbar, the optional side panel and the period: the events in their color, today marked in the day header and by the now line.

empty.changes_for_user: A period with no visible event shows the calendar icon, the title and the hint over the grid. The toolbar stays active and the week keeps its days.

loading.changes_for_user: Skeleton rows take the place of the events; the toolbar stays active and the week keeps its days. The events area is busy and the loading label is announced.

day-focus.token: scheduler/focus-border, scheduler/focus-border-width, scheduler/focus-border-radius, scheduler/focus-halo, scheduler/focus-halo-width, scheduler/focus-halo-radius
day-focus.changes_for_user: The keyboard focus on a day, the day header in the week and day views and the cell in the month, draws the focus border and the halo.

event-focus.changes_for_user: The keyboard focus on an event, on a month line, on a list row and on a cancelled event draws the same border and halo, in the color of the event.

event-hover.changes_for_user: The pointer over an event paints it one tone above; it does not move the focus or open the detail.

event-open.changes_for_user: The open event has the background of hover and aria-expanded true; the visible popover beside it is what says it is open.

event-cancelled.changes_for_user: A neutral body with an outline, no bar, the text Cancelled: before the struck title. With the keyboard focus, the border and the halo go outside the outline, in the color of the event.

today.token: scheduler/today-foreground, scheduler/today-indicator, scheduler/today-indicator-width, scheduler/now-indicator, scheduler/now-indicator-width, scheduler/now-indicator-size, scheduler/now-foreground
today.changes_for_user: Today has the number in color and a mark at the base of the day header; the now line with its dot crosses the column of today, with the current time in the time column.

business_rules: The piece is controlled: the screen owns events, calendars, the view and the date. The piece fires an event when the person acts and writes view, date, hide-side-panel, open-event and calendars as the person changes them; setting them from code fires nothing.
The color of an event is the color of its calendar: primary or one of the vertical colors. It is the choice of the person, equal in every brand, and never a status.
An instant is wall-clock text, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, and an all-day date is YYYY-MM-DD. A text with a time zone is refused, because the piece has no zone to read it in.
The piece does not draw the detail of an event. It hands the click to the screen and, when the screen puts content in the detail slot, opens the nph-popover beside the event.
Below 768 px of the width of the element the piece is the compact month with the list of the chosen day; the view select offers the same views and the compact month stays.

Each day and each event is a Tab stop, in the order of the document: toolbar, side panel, days from left to right, events in start order. There are no arrow keys on the grid; the mini month and the compact month keep the arrows of a date grid.
+N more goes to the day view of that date and gives the focus to the day.
The language of the dates is the nearest lang, crossing shadow roots; without one, en. The first day of the week is the property, not the language.
The height of an event comes from its duration, never below the minimum target; simultaneous events sit side by side and the title is cut on one line, whole in the accessible name.
The grid scrolls on its own: the toolbar and the day header stay in place, and the first view of a period is the hour of its first event, the now line or the early morning.
domain_errors: A view, a week-start, a date or a now that does not exist: the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause while it lasts.

An event with a repeated id, a start or end that does not exist, an end before the start, a time zone or a calendar that does not exist: the event is left out, with its own console.error in development.
A calendar with a repeated id, no name or a color outside the list: the calendar is left out, with its own console.error in development.
A label the piece needs and the screen did not give: it renders anyway and emits console.error in development, once, saying which keys are missing.

ai_hints: Use nph-scheduler to show the events of a calendar over time; to choose a date in a form use the date picker, and for tasks with no time use a list or a table.

Own the data: set events, calendars and labels, and change view and date when nph-view-change and nph-date-change fire. The piece writes them itself when the person acts, and fires nothing when code sets them.
Give every text the piece owes in labels, already localized, including the names read by the screen reader; a missing label renders and says which one.
Write each instant as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm and each all-day date as YYYY-MM-DD, with no time zone.
Give each calendar a color of the list: it is the choice of the person and never a status.
Open the detail on nph-event-click: put the content in the detail slot and set open-event to the id; the piece draws the popover, the focus and aria-expanded.
Create and edit events in the screen: nph-new-event and nph-day-click only say the day.
Set a height for the scheduler, or let the screen give it one, so the grid scrolls inside the piece.
Leave the phone alone: below 768 px the piece is the compact month and the same properties work.

accessibility.semantics: A section named by the period label. The event is a button whose name starts with its visible text, the Cancelled: prefix and the title, and carries the whole title, the time when it is written, the date, the time when it is not written, the calendar and, when it applies, cancelled and repeats; with a detail in the slot it has aria-haspopup dialog and aria-expanded. Each day of the grid is a button whose name starts with its visible text, the short weekday and the number, then the full date, with the word for today, and has aria-current date on today. The mini month and the compact month are a grid with column headers, and the list view has one heading per day and a list of rows. The avatars of the meetings carry the names of the people. A polite status announces the new period, and the loading label is a status while loading.
accessibility.accessible_name: The event: the visible text first (the Cancelled: prefix and the title, then the time when the row writes it), then the date, the time when the row does not write it, the calendar, cancelled and repeats, even when the title is cut with an ellipsis. The list row writes the time first, and the name follows. The day: the visible short weekday and number, then the full date, with the word for today. The icon buttons: the previous, next, new event and side panel labels. The view select: the view label.
keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab: the toolbar (sidebar button, Today, previous, next, view select, Filter, New event), then the side panel (mini month and My calendars), then the days from left to right, then the events in start order, left to right at the same start. Each day and each event is a Tab stop.
Enter and Space on an event: hand the click to the screen; with a detail in the slot, open it in the nph-popover and move the focus into it.

Esc with the detail open: close it and return the focus to the event. Esc with the view select or the Filter menu open: close the list and return the focus to the button. With nothing open it does nothing.
Enter and Space on +N more: go to the day view of that date and focus the day.

The arrow keys have no use on the grid. In the mini month and the compact month, the arrows move by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month, or by year with Shift, and Home and End to the start and the end of the week.
A press outside closes the detail and the focus stays where the person clicked.
accessibility.focus: The day, the event, the month and list rows and the cancelled event show the same border and halo, outside the part, in the color of the event: scheduler/focus-* in primary and scheduler/event-<color>-focus-* in the other colors. The toolbar buttons follow nph-button. Hover only paints the event and moves no focus.
accessibility.contrast: The title and the time of an event meet 4.5:1 on its background in both themes; the bar, the now line and the focus border meet 3:1. Today meets 4.5:1 on the card. The grid lines and the outline of the container are decoration.
accessibility.color_alternative: The cancelled event reads by Cancelled: and the struck title, besides the neutral body. Today reads by the number, the mark at the base of the day header, the now line and the word in the name of the day. The color of an event never carries meaning: the calendar name is in the accessible name.

invalid_combinations: A view outside work-week, week, day, month and list — the piece draws nothing.
A week-start outside sunday and monday — the piece draws nothing.
A date or a now that does not exist — the piece draws nothing.
An instant with a time zone — the event is left out.
Two events with the same id, or an end before the start — the event is left out.
A calendar color outside primary and the vertical colors — the calendar is left out.
educacao and primary together in the brand Educacao — they are the same color.
A color used as a status — the color is the choice of the calendar.
anti_patterns: Choosing a date in a form with the scheduler.
Using the color of an event as a status.
Showing a cancelled event only by color, or taking it out of the grid.
Two primary buttons in the toolbar: New event is the only one.
A divider between events in the week and day views: the line is only on the full hour.
Drawing the detail, or creating and editing the event, inside the piece.
Passing a time with a time zone, or writing the texts of the piece by hand in another place than labels.
Relying on the arrow keys on the grid: each day and each event is a Tab stop.
